Every statement and connection

121 statements and 92 connections, in the order of the six questions. Open one to see where it sits, who contributed it, who accepted it, and a brief for your AI.

Question 1What are we trying to achieve? See the diagram →

GoalAccepted for nowA reason commons is emerging and widely used: people, with AI, build shared tree-structured reasoning (such as Logical Thinking Process maps) and weave it into discussion and work, so discourse is more constructive and people find the leverage points and achieve their goals together far more effectively.Accepted for now by Rufus Pollock
← All statementsWhat are we trying to achieve?
GoalAccepted for now

A reason commons is emerging and widely used: people, with AI, build shared tree-structured reasoning (such as Logical Thinking Process maps) and weave it into discussion and work, so discourse is more constructive and people find the leverage points and achieve their goals together far more effectively.

Shown in diagrams as: “A reason commons of AI-supported, tree-structured reasoning is widely used.”

Where it sits

Contributed by
Original contributor not identified and AI assistant
Accepted for now by
Rufus Pollock
Recorded context
No acceptance date was recorded.

Connections

  • Leads into · is needed forAI-supported tools make creating and revising reasoning trees easy, whether people build them explicitly or the trees are drawn semi-automatically from their existing discussion.
  • Leads into · is needed forReasoning trees improve discussion where it already happens (chats, documents, meetings, social platforms), surfacing the relevant structure alongside the conversation.
  • Leads into · is needed forReal people and groups use it regularly and see better decisions and results, starting with Rufus, David and Second Renaissance.
  • Leads into · is needed forIt is valuable to one person or a pair from day one, without needing a commons first, and gets more valuable for a team, an organization and the wider world.
  • Leads into · is needed forTrees are published, connected and evolved collectively, within organizations and in public, so people build on each other's reasoning, share core reference trees, and find others working toward the same goals.

History

  • Added in the release of 27 October 2026

Question: Who does what?

Starting needs the exact skill set up, a real investment of time, and someone explaining the method, even with AI.

AND
Write a short start guide for AI-only participants (installing the skill, the first prompt) and try it on a fresh setup before their sessions.
produces
AI-only participants start their sessions without our help, so T2 compares the guidance rather than the setup.

Question: Who does what?
Item: tt2-l-priced-offer (Connection)

Six people, including a pair or small group, agree and book in time to hold the sessions by 22 Nov.
AND
A tested answer to who pays for what; there is none yet (G4).
AND
Make a priced offer within Stage 1, one paid session or a priced pilot.

A first signal on who pays, from someone accepting or declining the offer, and their reasons.
